newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major says folly to let BOE set rates.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major says folly to let BOE set rates.

text.p: Former British Prime Minister John Major said the new Labour government's decision to let the Bank of England set interest rates was folly.
In an interview with BBC Radio Four, he cited this as one of the serious mistakes by the new government that would become apparent in the months ahead.
"I think the decision to give independence to the Bank of England was folly," Major said.

"The Chancellor of the Exchequer has thrown away one of the key economic levers that were in his hand. I don't believe that is prudent. I wouldn't have done it and I think it was a mistake for him to do it."
New Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown relinquished the right to set interest rates within days of the May 1 election, ceding it to a new monetary policy committee at the Bank of England.
